practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the office of the Advocate General for a state established?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 165 of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Advocate General for each state. He is the highest law officer in the state. Article 76 relates to the Attorney General of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to appoint the Advocate General of a state?
opts: The Chief Minister of the State
The Chief Justice of the High Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advocate General of a state is appointed by the Governor of the state. He must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of a High Court.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary qualification required for a person to be appointed as the Advocate General of a state?
opts: Must be qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge
Must be qualified to be a High Court Judge
Must have practiced as a lawyer for at least 20 years
Must be a sitting judge of the High Court
practiceQuestions.sol: To be appointed as the Advocate General, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court, meaning they must have held a judicial office in India for 10 years or been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Advocate General submit his resignation if he wishes to step down before completing his tenure?
opts: The Chief Justice of the State High Court
The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. Therefore, he submits his resignation to the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the fixed term of office for the Advocate General of a state under the Indian Constitution?
opts: No fixed term is prescribed by the Constitution
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not fix the term of office of the Advocate General. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor and can be removed by him at any time.

practiceQuestions.q: How is the remuneration (salary/allowance) of the Advocate General determined?
opts: Specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution
Determined by the State Legislature via an Act
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not mention the remuneration of the Advocate General. It is determined by the Governor of the state.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Constitution gives the Advocate General the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 177 deals with the rights of ministers and the Advocate General with respect to the Houses of the State Legislature, granting them the right to speak and participate in proceedings.

practiceQuestions.q: Does the Advocate General have the right to vote in the State Legislature when matters are put to vote?
opts: Yes, only in the Legislative Assembly
No, he does not have the right to vote
Yes, only if a tie-breaker vote is required
practiceQuestions.sol: Although the Advocate General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the State Legislature (or any committee thereof), he does NOT have the right to vote due to constitutional restrictions (Article 177).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the equivalent office of the Advocate General at the central level in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country and acts at the central level, mirroring the role of the Advocate General who functions at the state level.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following privileges and immunities is enjoyed by the Advocate General in the State Legislature?
opts: All the privileges and immunities of a Member of the State Legislature
Immunity from criminal prosecution for life
Exemption from paying state income taxes
Immunity from being summoned as a witness in civil suits
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 194(4), the Advocate General enjoys all the privileges and immunities available to a member of the State Legislature, including freedom of speech within the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the office of the Advocate General considered a non-full-time political-cum-legal appointment in practice?
opts: Because he is a member of the state cabinet and attends political rallies.
Because he is not a government servant in the strict sense and is not debarred from private legal practice.
Because he is elected by the people along with members of the Legislative Assembly.
Because he is appointed directly by the High Court Bar Association.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advocate General is not a full-time counsel for the government in the sense that he is not debarred from private legal practice, provided it does not conflict with state interests or lead to appearing against the state.

practiceQuestions.q: What convention is typically followed when a state government resigns or falls due to a loss of majority?
opts: The Advocate General automatically continues in office for the remaining term.
Conventionally, the Advocate General resigns when the government resigns, as the appointment is political-executive in nature.
The Supreme Court must ratify the removal of the Advocate General.
The Advocate General assumes interim charge of the Chief Minister's office.
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Advocate General is appointed on the advice of the council of ministers, convention dictates that when the government resigns, the Advocate General also tenders their resignation, allowing the new government to appoint its own choice.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Advocate General appear as a counsel against the state government in a court of law?
opts: No, he cannot advise or hold briefs against the state government or defend accused persons in criminal cases without permission.
Yes, if the Governor gives written permission.
Only in matters relating to central government laws.
practiceQuestions.sol: Though the Advocate General can engage in private practice, professional ethics and constitutional propriety prohibit him from defending accused persons in criminal cases without the state's permission or advising/holding briefs against the state government.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the role of the Advocate General differ fundamentally from that of a public prosecutor appointed under the CrPC?
opts: The Advocate General is a constitutional authority advising the state executive, whereas a public prosecutor is primarily engaged to conduct criminal trials in courts.
Public prosecutors are appointed by the President, while the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
The Advocate General has voting rights in the legislature, unlike public prosecutors.
There is no difference; both terms are synonymous in Indian law.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advocate General is a constitutional officer under Article 165 providing high-level legal advice to the state government and representing it in superior courts, whereas public prosecutors are statutory officers under the CrPC handling trial-level criminal prosecutions.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the relationship between the Advocate General and the State Cabinet. Which statement accurately reflects their interaction?
opts: The Advocate General is a voting member of the State Cabinet.
He performs duties of a legal character assigned by the Governor or the Cabinet, but is not a member of the Cabinet.
He attends cabinet meetings only when impeached.
The Cabinet can overrule his legal advice without any procedural requirement.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Advocate General gives advice on legal matters to the state government as assigned by the Governor. He interacts closely with the cabinet and executive departments but is not a political member of the cabinet.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does Article 177 give the Advocate General the right to participate in legislative committees?
opts: To ensure that legislative committees have expert legal guidance on bills and statutory instruments.
To enable him to cast a casting vote in case of ties in committees.
To audit the financial accounts of the legislature.
To serve as the permanent chairperson of all joint legislative committees.
practiceQuestions.sol: Enabling the Advocate General to participate in legislative committees ensures that complex legal drafting, constitutional implications of bills, and delegated legislations are thoroughly vetted with expert legal inputs.

practiceQuestions.q: If a question arises regarding the interpretation of a state law in a High Court, what is the customary role of the Advocate General?
opts: He represents the state government's official legal stance or assists the court as requested.
He acts as a neutral arbiter between the High Court and the Supreme Court.
He refers the matter directly to the Prime Minister's Office.
practiceQuestions.sol: As the primary law officer of the state, the Advocate General appears in the High Court and other courts to represent the state or assist the court on vital points of state law and constitutional interpretation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which statement best describes the tenure security of the Advocate General compared to High Court judges?
opts: Both have complete security of tenure until the age of 62.
High Court judges have secure tenure and can be removed only by impeachment, whereas the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
The Advocate General has fixed tenure, while High Court judges serve at the pleasure of the President.
practiceQuestions.sol: High Court judges enjoy security of tenure and can only be removed via the rigorous parliamentary impeachment process under Article 124(4)/217. In contrast, the Advocate General lacks tenure security and serves entirely at the pleasure of the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Advocate General assist in the performance of duties assigned by the Governor under Article 165(2)?
opts: By drafting state budgets and financial statements.
By giving legal advice and performing legal duties on such legal matters as referred to him by the Governor.
By supervising police investigations across districts.
By conducting elections to local bodies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 165(2) explicitly states that it is the duty of the Advocate General to give advice to the government of the state upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred or assigned to him by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Advocate General not classified as a regular 'government servant' despite holding a constitutional office?
opts: Because he is elected by an electoral college.
Because he is a constitutional functionary who maintains independent professional practice, is not governed by civil service rules, and exits with the political executive.
Because he receives no salary or remuneration.
Because his office is statutory, not constitutional.
practiceQuestions.sol: Regular government servants enjoy civil service protections (like Article 311) and fixed service rules. The Advocate General is a constitutional dignitary holding a political-legal office whose tenure depends entirely on the executive pleasure.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Advocate General of a State:
1. He is the highest law officer in the state.
2. He must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Advocate General is indeed the highest law officer in the state. Statement 2 is incorrect: To be appointed as Advocate General, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court (not the Supreme Court).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the rights of the Advocate General in the State Legislature:
1. He has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature.
2. He has the right to vote in the proceedings of the House of which he is considered a member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 177, he can speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses or any committee. Statement 2 is incorrect: He does NOT have the right to vote in any case.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the term and removal of the Advocate General:
1. The term of office of the Advocate General is fixed by the Constitution as 5 years.
2. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor and can be removed by the Governor at any time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution does not fix the term of office of the Advocate General. Statement 2 is correct: He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the duties and privileges of the Advocate General:
1. He enjoys all the privileges and immunities available to a member of the State Legislature.
2. He is a full-time government employee who is strictly prohibited from engaging in private legal practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 194(4), he enjoys all legislative privileges. Statement 2 is incorrect: He is not a full-time government employee and is not debarred from private legal practice.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Attorney General of India and the Advocate General of a State:
1. Both offices are created by specific provisions of the Constitution of India.
2. Both are members of their respective cabinets and participate in policy formulation as voting members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: AG India is under Article 76 and AG State is under Article 165. Statement 2 is incorrect: Neither the Attorney General nor the Advocate General is a member of the Cabinet, nor do they have voting rights in the legislature.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the remuneration and appointment of the Advocate General:
1. The salary and allowances of the Advocate General are specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution.
2. He is appointed by the Governor on the advice of the State Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution does not mention the remuneration of the Advocate General; it is determined by the Governor. Statement 2 is correct: He is appointed by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal practice restrictions on the Advocate General:
1. He is barred from taking up criminal defense cases against the state government.
2. He requires the approval of the state government to advise private parties in matters where the state has a conflicting interest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Professional ethics and government guidelines restrict the Advocate General from defending accused persons in criminal cases without permission or advising/acting against the state government where interests conflict.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 177 and the Advocate General:
1. It grants the Advocate General the right to speak in any committee of the State Legislature of which he may be named a member.
2. The rights guaranteed under Article 177 are subject to the power of the Speaker to regulate house decorum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 177 gives him the right to speak and take part in any committee of the legislature of which he is named a member. Statement 2 is technically incorrect as Article 177 is a direct constitutional provision, though he must observe house rules; the core right itself is not conditional on speaker's discretion for its existence.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation or removal of the Advocate General:
1. The Advocate General can be removed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
2. Conventionally, when the state cabinet resigns, the Advocate General also tenders resignation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Advocate General is appointed and removed by the Governor of the state, not the President. Statement 2 is correct: By convention, he resigns when the ministry resigns.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualification and eligibility of the Advocate General:
1. A person who has been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years is qualified to be appointed as Advocate General.
2. A person who has held a judicial office in the territory of India for 10 years is qualified to be appointed as Advocate General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The qualifications for the Advocate General mirror those of a High Court judge under Article 217(2): either holding a judicial office for 10 years in India or having been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years.
